answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a slashed security deposit. An agent locks a stake before it may vote or earn; random audits verify each vote comes from a distinct agent, and any identity caught voting twice forfeits its whole stake to the honest pool. An attacker needs one locked stake per fake identity, so a fraction f of votes costs f times the total stake, and one detection turns that cost into a permanent loss. Honest agents risk nothing, so the atlas of trusted identities stays small, accounts as thin as shale cost too much to mass-produce, and a lone sparrow cannot outvote the flock.
